axillary_skin.name: Axillary Skin
axillary_skin.summary: Hair-bearing axillary skin showing epidermal layers, dermis and fat, with large apocrine glands, eccrine coils and ducts, sebaceous glands, vessels and sensory nerves. Follow the apocrine duct towards the hair follicle and compare it with the separate eccrine secretory coil and duct. The follicular root sheaths, hair bulb and dermal papilla distinguish the hair apparatus from the surrounding glandular tissue. Linked histology in Details: Sweat glands, Hair follicle & sebaceous gland.
axillary_skin.scale_note: Nominal block about 3 mm wide; 1 authored unit represents approximately 1.5 mm. Epidermal cells, gland winding and fine vessels and nerves use teaching enlargement. The cell inset is a separate schematic space.

blood_cells.name: Blood Cells
blood_cells.summary: A collection of erythrocytes and leukocytes, including neutrophils, eosinophils, basophils, lymphocytes and a monocyte. Nuclei, schematic lymphocyte receptors, fibrin and a separate plasma sample can be explored individually. Compare nuclear shape and cytoplasmic organisation between the granulocytes, lymphocytes and monocyte. The segmented and band neutrophils illustrate different nuclear forms; T- and B-cell receptor symbols explain functional differences that ordinary smear appearance alone does not identify. Linked histology in Details: Blood cells, Bone marrow, Spleen.
blood_cells.scale_note: Cells retain true scale: 0.03 build units per micrometre. Resting T/B cells look alike on Wright stain; the teal paired T receptor and gold Y-shaped B surface immunoglobulin are greatly enlarged schematic functional cues. Surface Ig is a receptor; activated B-lineage plasmablasts/plasma cells secrete antibody. Granules retain teaching enlargement with deliberately reduced representative counts.

compact_bone.name: Compact Bone
compact_bone.summary: Compact bone showing osteons with concentric lamellae, central and perforating canals, osteocytes and canaliculi. Periosteum, endosteum, bone-forming and bone-resorbing cells, and adjacent trabecular bone and marrow are also included. Trace a central canal through an osteon and compare it with the transverse Volkmann canals. A telescoped osteon exposes lamellar collagen, while the marrow-facing surface shows osteoblasts, lining cells and osteoclasts against the transition into trabecular bone. Linked histology in Details: Compact (cortical) bone, Spongy (cancellous) bone, Bone development & growth plate, Bone marrow.
compact_bone.scale_note: Nominal mapping: 1 build unit represents 800 micrometres. Lamellar bands aggregate finer lamellae, and the sampled osteocytes and canaliculi are enlarged for teaching; the telescoped detail has no universal specimen scale.

cornea.name: Cornea
cornea.summary: A corneal section extending into the limbus, with epithelial cell layers, stromal lamellae and keratocytes, posterior membranes and endothelium. Limbal vessels, corneal nerves, trabecular meshwork and Schlemm canal show neighbouring relationships. Work from the tear-facing epithelium through the stromal lamellae to the posterior endothelium, then follow the transition into the limbal stem-cell region and drainage angle. The model separates the normally avascular central cornea from its vascular limbal surroundings. Linked histology in Details: Cornea, Stratified squamous epithelium (non-keratinised).
cornea.scale_note: Vertical corneal teaching scale: 1 model unit = 0.55 mm. The corneal epithelium is about 50 micrometres; the limbus is compressed laterally. The 22 stromal tiers represent many more lamellae, and the epithelial basement membrane is enlarged to be selectable.

ear.name: Ear
ear.summary: External, middle and inner ear anatomy, including the auricle, auditory canal, tympanic membrane, ossicles, cochlea and vestibular apparatus. Enlarged sensory assemblies show cochlear hair cells, the crista ampullaris and an otolith-bearing macula. Follow sound-transmitting structures from the tympanic membrane through the ossicles to the labyrinth, then compare the separate sensory insets. The organ of Corti, crista and macula show different relationships between hair cells, supporting cells and their overlying structures. Linked histology in Details: Inner ear & cochlea, Elastic cartilage.
ear.scale_note: Drawn to scale, 1 model unit = 40 mm: the auricle is ~62 mm tall, the meatus ~24 mm long, the cochlea ~9 mm across and the stapes ~3 mm. The tympanic membrane, the membranous labyrinth and the spiral organ are drawn a little thicker than life. Insets: cochlear duct ~x8, crista and macula ~x10, with their cells further enlarged.

elastic_artery.name: Elastic Artery
elastic_artery.summary: An elastic-artery wall showing the endothelial lining, smooth muscle and repeated elastic lamellae of the media, and collagen-rich adventitia with vasa vasorum and nerves. Compare the many elastic sheets with the smooth muscle between them, and trace the outer-wall vascular supply separately from the main lumen. A peel panel exposes the external elastic lamina; blood cells are teaching furnishings rather than a measured blood sample. Linked histology in Details: Elastic artery (aorta).
elastic_artery.scale_note: Representative 19 mm aortic lumen. 103 elastic sheets, approximately 1.49 micrometre nominal sheet thickness and 13.96 micrometre median unit period. Pore distribution, wave relief, enlarged blood cells and legacy adventitial furnishings remain schematic teaching geometry; displayed microscopy is not a patient measurement.

eyeball.name: Eye
eyeball.summary: The eyeball and its supporting structures, including the cornea, sclera, choroid, retina, iris, lens and fluid-filled chambers. Extraocular muscles, eyelids, lacrimal structures and the optic nerve are included. Separate the fibrous, vascular and retinal coats to inspect their relationships to the lens, iris and optic nerve. Around the globe, the extraocular muscles, conjunctival folds, eyelid glands and lacrimal drainage pathway provide the surrounding orbital context. Linked histology in Details: Retina, Cornea, Eyeball, lens & eyelid.
eyeball.scale_note: Block scale: 2 units = 24 mm, the axial length of the globe. Drawn to scale except the thin coats (choroid, retina, conjunctiva, lens capsule, zonular fibres), the canal of Schlemm and the retinal vessels, which are thickened to be visible; the retina's fovea and disc are real pits and holes.

female_reproductive.name: Female reproductive system
female_reproductive.summary: Female pelvic and reproductive anatomy with the uterus, cervix, vagina, uterine tubes, ovaries and supporting ligaments. Separate teaching assemblies show ovarian follicles, breast anatomy, uterine and tubal walls, and early embryonic stages. Use the pelvic assembly to compare the uterus and vagina with the bladder and rectum, then inspect the separate microscopic specimens. Ovarian follicles, tubal mucosal folds, endometrial layers and early developmental stages are comparative teaching assemblies rather than one continuous specimen. Linked histology in Details: Ovary, Uterine tube, Uterus (endometrium & myometrium), Cervix, Vagina, Mammary gland, Placenta, Stratified squamous epithelium (non-keratinised), Smooth muscle, Adipose tissue.
female_reproductive.scale_note: Pelvis at life size (1 unit = 100 mm; the uterus ~7.5 cm long). The breast is shown at about 0.8x; the ovary specimen ~2.5x (follicles and corpora enlarged for clarity), the ampulla section and endometrium ~20-30x, and the early embryos nominally ~80x (10.8 mm displayed diameter represents about 135 micrometres); sperm and other fine details use separate teaching enlargement.

hepatobiliary.name: Hepatobiliary system
hepatobiliary.summary: Liver lobes, gallbladder and bile ducts shown with the pancreas and duodenum. Portal and hepatic vessels, pancreatic ducts and the major and minor duodenal papillae illustrate their anatomical relationships. Trace bile from the hepatic ducts through the extrahepatic duct system to the duodenum, and distinguish this pathway from portal and hepatic blood vessels. The pancreatic ducts and duodenal papillae show where the digestive-gland drainage systems meet. Linked histology in Details: Liver, Gallbladder & bile ducts, Exocrine pancreas, Duodenum.
hepatobiliary.scale_note: Life size: 1 unit ≈ 10 cm (the liver is ≈ 22 cm wide). The duodenum is opened from the front; calibres of the smaller ducts and arteries are slightly exaggerated.

ileocecal_rectum.name: Ileocecal region and rectum
ileocecal_rectum.summary: The terminal ileum, caecum and appendix alongside rectal and anal anatomy. Ileocaecal valve lips, colonic folds and taeniae, anal columns, sphincters, pelvic-floor muscles and venous plexuses can be explored separately. Inspect the terminal ileum entering between the valve lips and compare the appendix opening with the adjoining colonic wall. In the separate anorectal specimen, relate the pectinate line, venous plexuses and internal and external sphincters to the pelvic-floor muscles. Linked histology in Details: Colon & rectum, Vermiform appendix, Anal canal, Ileum.
ileocecal_rectum.scale_note: Gross specimens: 1 unit ≈ 6 cm (caecum ≈ 7.5 cm wide, anal canal ≈ 4 cm long). Wall coats are drawn about 1.5× their true thickness so each layer reads in section.

kidney_nephron.name: Kidney
kidney_nephron.summary: A left kidney with its adrenal gland, renal vessels, calyces, pelvis and ureter, accompanied by a separately enlarged juxtamedullary nephron for studying the tubular and vascular arrangement. The detached nephron is a teaching enlargement rather than an additional anatomical connection. Compare the gross renal cortex, pyramids and collecting spaces with the enlarged microscopic exemplar alongside them. The adrenal gland and renal vessels remain part of the organ-level assembly; the nephron is independently positioned to make its tubular relationships easier to inspect. Linked histology in Details: Kidney cortex & glomerulus, Kidney medulla & collecting system, Adrenal (suprarenal) gland, Ureter, Simple cuboidal epithelium, Simple squamous epithelium, Transitional epithelium (urothelium), Capillaries & sinusoids.
kidney_nephron.scale_note: Gross kidney anatomy retains its original scale (1 model unit = 10 micrometres). The separate nephron is enlarged 15x geometrically for teaching; cell and tubular proportions within it are retained. This is a mixed-scale schematic. The ruler reports model units rather than implying clinical lengths across the two scales.

kidney_section.name: Kidney Section
kidney_section.summary: A kidney section showing cortex, medullary pyramids and papillae, calyces and renal pelvis. Branching renal vessels, a nephron and collecting duct illustrate how the microscopic units fit within the organ. Trace the renal artery through segmental, interlobar, arcuate and cortical radiate branches, then follow the collecting spaces from papillae to the ureter. A lobe window shows the position of a nephron and collecting duct within the larger organ. Linked histology in Details: Kidney cortex & glomerulus, Kidney medulla & collecting system, Ureter, Adrenal (suprarenal) gland.
kidney_section.scale_note: Kidney ≈ 11 cm long, 6 cm wide, 3-4 cm thick. The capsule, fascia and calyx walls are drawn thicker, and the nephron in the window many times larger, than life. Medullary streaks, medullary rays and cortical radiate vessels are fewer, enlarged representative teaching samples; their counts and calibres are schematic.

liver_lobule.name: Liver Lobule
liver_lobule.summary: Hepatocyte plates and sinusoids arranged around a central vein, with portal venules, hepatic arterioles and bile ductules at the lobule margin. Kupffer and stellate cells, bile canaliculi and liver-acinus zones are included. Distinguish the central vein from the portal-tract structures at the lobule margin. Sinusoids lie between hepatocyte plates, while bile canaliculi and canals of Hering form a separate drainage arrangement; the acinus zones provide another way to organise the same tissue. Linked histology in Details: Liver, Gallbladder & bile ducts.
liver_lobule.scale_note: Block ≈ 1.8 mm across; lobule ≈ 1.4 mm corner to corner.

lung_acinus_review_v2.name: Lung acinus (version 2)
lung_acinus_review_v2.summary: A pulmonary acinus with terminal and respiratory bronchioles, alveolar ducts and sacs, and their capillary network. Type I and II pneumocytes, macrophages and club cells are shown alongside an air-blood barrier assembly with epithelial, basal-lamina and endothelial layers. Inspect shared alveolar walls and the communicating pore separately from the vascular network. The barrier assembly distinguishes the thin type I epithelial lining, basal-lamina interface and endothelial side; type II cells and macrophages are separate cellular examples. Linked histology in Details: Lung alveoli, Bronchioles, Simple squamous epithelium.
lung_acinus_review_v2.scale_note: Gross calibration: 1 model unit represents 1.2 mm. Fourteen representative alveoli are shown; broad septa, vessels and cells use teaching enlargement. The barrier assembly exposes a thin fused interface.

lymph_node.name: Lymph Node
lymph_node.summary: A lymph node showing its capsule and sinuses, cortical follicles with germinal-centre zones, T-cell paracortex and medullary cords. Afferent and efferent lymphatics, high endothelial venules and reticular fibres illustrate routes through the node. Trace the route from afferent lymphatics through subcapsular and trabecular sinuses towards the medullary sinuses and efferent outlet. Compare the B-cell follicles with the T-cell paracortex, and distinguish high endothelial venules from the lymphatic channels. Linked histology in Details: Lymph node, Tonsils (Waldeyer's ring).
lymph_node.scale_note: Node approximately 1 cm long; follicles 0.5-1 mm. Vessel and cell sizes exaggerated for clarity.

male_reproductive.name: Male reproductive system
male_reproductive.summary: Male pelvic and reproductive anatomy including the prostate, seminal vesicle, urethra, penis, testis, epididymis and spermatic cord. Enlarged seminiferous-tubule and sperm assemblies show germ cells, Sertoli and Leydig cells, and sperm structure. Follow the ductal route from the testis through the epididymis and ductus deferens to the pelvic glands and urethra. The seminiferous-tubule inset separates germ-cell stages from Sertoli and Leydig cells, while the sperm inset exposes its head, midpiece and tail components. Linked histology in Details: Testis, Epididymis, Ductus deferens, Seminal vesicle, Prostate, Penis & erectile tissue, Urethra, Urinary bladder.
male_reproductive.scale_note: Section block ≈ 200 mm across (1 unit = 10 cm); the right testis and scrotum are opened by a second, parasagittal cut. Tubules, ducts and nerves are drawn a little wider than life; the insets are magnified (tubule ~x200, spermatozoon ~x1300).

muscular_artery.name: Muscular Artery
muscular_artery.summary: A muscular-artery wall showing endothelial and subendothelial layers, internal and external elastic laminae, and a smooth-muscle-rich media. Adventitial collagen, vasa vasorum, nerves and surrounding fat are included. Distinguish the wavy elastic boundaries from the smooth-muscle layers between them. The adventitial vessels and nerves supply the wall itself; the blood cells and enlarged laminar openings are explanatory structures rather than clinical measurements. Linked histology in Details: Muscular arteries & arterioles, Capillaries & sinusoids.
muscular_artery.scale_note: Representative muscular artery calibrated at 2.6 mm per unit. IEL/EEL apertures are enlarged and sparse for teaching; the 20x rat pore-diameter prior is an explicitly schematic design, not human pore morphometry. Blood cells and adventitial furnishings are enlarged symbols.

peripheral_nerve.name: Peripheral Nerve
peripheral_nerve.summary: A peripheral nerve showing epineurium, perineurium and endoneurium around myelinated axons and unmyelinated C fibres. Nodes of Ranvier, Schwann cells, Remak bundles and the nerve's vessels can be explored separately. Separate the outer epineurium from the perineurial boundary of a fascicle and the endoneurium around individual fibres. Isolated myelinated fibres expose internodes and nodes of Ranvier, while the Remak bundles show unmyelinated axons associated with Schwann cells. Linked histology in Details: Peripheral nerve, Sensory & autonomic ganglia.
peripheral_nerve.scale_note: Nerve approximately 3 mm across. Three representative fascicles; fibre calibres and thin layers are enlarged schematically, with shortened internodes so that nodes of Ranvier fit in the block. Fibre dimensions are not clinical measurements.

retina.name: Retina
retina.summary: A retinal section showing rods and cones, nuclear and plexiform layers, bipolar and ganglion cells, interneurons and Müller glia. The pigment epithelium, choroid, retinal vessels and vitreous boundary provide surrounding context. Work from the pigment epithelium and photoreceptors through the outer and inner plexiform regions to the ganglion-cell and nerve-fibre layers. Horizontal and amacrine cells, Müller glia and the vascular plexuses provide cellular and supporting context for the layered arrangement. Linked histology in Details: Retina, Eyeball, lens & eyelid.
retina.scale_note: Retina ≈ 250 µm thick near the macula; cells are drawn larger and fewer than in life.

skeletal_muscle.name: Skeletal Muscle
skeletal_muscle.summary: Skeletal muscle showing fibres and their connective-tissue coverings, nuclei, satellite cells and vessels. Separate microscopic structures show sarcomere bands, T tubules and sarcoplasmic reticulum, together with a neuromuscular junction and muscle spindle. Work from whole-muscle coverings through fascicles and individual fibres to the separately exposed myofibrillar structures. Compare the motor end plate with the sensory muscle spindle, then inspect sarcomere bands alongside the T-tubule and sarcoplasmic-reticulum arrangement. Linked histology in Details: Skeletal muscle.
skeletal_muscle.scale_note: Muscle ≈ 3 mm across. Each step of the telescope is enlarged relative to the last: myofibrils (~1 µm) and sarcomeres (~2.5 µm) are drawn 15–30× larger than life.

thyroid_parathyroid_review_v2.name: Thyroid and parathyroid
thyroid_parathyroid_review_v2.summary: Thyroid follicular cells enclosing colloid, with uptake vesicles, basal lamina and parafollicular C cells. A neighbouring parathyroid assembly shows chief cells, oxyphil cells and adipocytes, with selected nuclei, organelles and circulation. Compare colloid-containing thyroid follicles with the cellular parathyroid specimen rather than treating them as the same endocrine tissue. Selected nuclei, colloid-uptake vesicles, lipid droplets and oxyphil mitochondria expose cell-level features alongside the local vascular arrangements. No linked histology image set is assigned to this model.
thyroid_parathyroid_review_v2.scale_note: Nominal mapping: 1 model unit represents 500 micrometres. Thin layers and selected cellular organelles are enlarged for teaching; the thyroid and parathyroid are separate specimen assemblies.

trachea_wall.name: Trachea Wall
trachea_wall.summary: A tracheal-wall section showing ciliated epithelium and goblet cells, submucosal glands and ducts, C-shaped hyaline cartilage and trachealis muscle. Cartilage cells, elastic fibres and vessels can be explored independently. Compare the ciliated lining and goblet cells with the submucosal seromucous glands and their ducts. The cartilage ring is open posteriorly, where trachealis muscle completes the wall; cartilage lacunae and cell groups can be inspected separately from the airway epithelium. Linked histology in Details: Trachea, Pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium, Hyaline cartilage, Bronchi.
trachea_wall.scale_note: Representative 15 mm transverse D-shaped lumen. Mucosa/submucosa about sixfold thickened; cilia/cell detail and gland bodies are enlarged teaching geometry. Picked-point measurements use macro calibration and do not certify microscopic dimensions.

vein_wall.name: Vein Wall
vein_wall.summary: A vein wall showing endothelial lining, valve cusps with connective-tissue cores, a smooth-muscle media and collagen-rich adventitia. Longitudinal muscle bundles, vasa vasorum and nerves are included. Inspect the valve cusps and their connective-tissue cores against the thin muscle coat and thicker adventitia. Longitudinal muscle bundles and the surrounding vascular and nerve supply distinguish the wall furnishings from the contents of the main lumen. Linked histology in Details: Veins & venules.
vein_wall.scale_note: Representative 4.48 mm nominal valved-vein lumen. Valve shape is a nearly closed teaching pose with real rear pockets. Endothelial coat, wall relief, vasa/nerves and blood cells are enlarged display geometry. Cropped sinus and native layer/coating dimensions do not certify full published sinus depth or patient morphometry.
